name: Durak Severnyi (Northern Durak)
description: Durak Severnyi (Northern Fool) is an atmospheric and high-stakes variant of the Russian card game Durak, primarily played in the Northern regions of Russia and Siberia. While it follows the standard Podkidnoy (throw-in) mechanics for the majority of the game, it contains a legendary 'sting in the tail': a late-game trump suit shift. By hiding the final trump identity until the very last card is drawn, Durak Severnyi forces players to maintain a balanced hand of all suits, as a dominant lead in the initial trump suit can instantly turn into a liability at the game's climax.

history.origins: Originating in the Arkhangelsk and Vologda regions, this variant reflected the unpredictable and harsh nature of the Northern Russian climate. It was designed to prevent 'trump hoarding'â€”a common strategy in standard Durak that can make the endgame predictable.
timeline: 19th Century: Simple Durak variants adapt to regional preferences in Northern trade hubs.
1940s-50s: Modern Severnyi rules with the 'secret trump' element become popular in military and labor outposts.
Present: Maintained as a cult variant for players who find standard Durak too predictable.
history.cultural: Symbolizes the 'Northern Temperament'â€”patience followed by a sudden, game-changing shift in fortune.
history.evolution: Evolution from a game of attrition to a game of high-risk probability where the endgame landscape shift is the central focus.

setup.players: 2-6 players. Best with 3-4 to ensure the Secret Trump phase is reached.
setup.deck: 36-card Russian pack (6, 7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A).
setup.dealing:
1. Each player is dealt 6 cards.
2. One card is placed FACE-DOWN in the center.
3. The next card is placed FACE-UP on top of it (The Initial Trump Suit).
4. The stock is placed on top of these two cards.

rules.objective: Escape the 'Fool' (Durak) title by shedding all cards, especially during the chaotic trump-shift endgame.
rules.gameplay:
1. Standard Play: Follow Podkidnoy rules (Attacking, Defending, Throw-ins).
2. Initial Trump: Use the face-up card suit for the first phase.
3. The Shift: When the stock is empty, the player who draws the LAST (face-down) card reveals it.
4. New Reality: The suit of that final card IMMEDIATELY becomes the new trump suit for the rest of the game.
keyRules: The change of trump suit happens instantly; currently active attacks are resolved using the NEW suit.
If the face-down card matches the initial trump suit, nothing changes (a 'lucky North').

strategy.basic: Do not burn all your non-trump high cards (Aces/Kings) early. In Severnyi, those 'junk' cards might become trumps in the final five minutes of the game.
strategy.intermediate: Hand Diversification: Unlike standard Durak where you want to empty yourself of non-trump suits, in Severnyi, you should try to keep at least one high card of every suit until the final card is revealed.
strategy.advanced: Counting the Talon: Track how many cards are left in the stock. If you are the one about to draw the final card, try to ensure you have a hand that benefits from a 'random' suit becoming trumps.
tips: Revealing the final card is a massive tactical moment. If you are the one revealed it, you have the first knowledge of the new landscapeâ€”use it to attack effectively.
If you held the 6 of the initial trump suit (allowing you to exchange for the face-up card), do so early; it won't be worth much if the suit changes.

variations.name: Secret Trump (Trump Shift)
variations.description: After the face-up trump is drawn as second-to-last from the stock, the player who draws the final face-down card reveals it; that card's suit becomes the new trump for the rest of the game; the former trump becomes an ordinary suit. If the face-down card is the same suit as the initial trump, nothing changes.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Secret trump is the core rule set; no engine overrides needed for this variant.
